preregistered.decision: is the tile rung's best scorer good enough to be the generative loop's scoring head?
preregistered.bar_a_meaning: the primary scorer realises at least half the AVAILABLE selection value
preregistered.bar_b_margin_is_noise_aware: the effective margin is max(0.10, 2 * permutation-null stdev at that seed and k) -- a flat 0.10 is the SAME ORDER as the measured scorer-realisation spread (0.096), so alone it could be cleared by noise
preregistered.bar_b_meaning: the scorer earns its keep IN THE LOOP, not only on correlation
preregistered.thresholds_are: ASSERTED, not derived; the per-trial ceiling arm that normalises them IS derived
preregistered.mirrors: scripts/glm_oracle_selection.py (designed grid): bar A 0.50, bar B max(0.10, 2*sd)

comparison_anchor.note: cross-AXIS means over 5 element axes; this run reports cross-SEED means over 10 leave-peak-out splits. Different pooling units -- compare with that in mind.

verdicts.ORACLE_READY_AS_SCORING_HEAD: bar A and bar B both pass on a majority of seeds -- further prediction work has measured diminishing returns FOR THE GENERATIVE GOAL
verdicts.CRUDE_BASELINE_SUFFICES: bar A passes, bar B fails -- GC does the work; the biophysical scorer is not what the loop is waiting for
verdicts.SELECTION_IS_THE_BOTTLENECK: bar A fails -- the scoring head cannot convert its correlation into a choice, so prediction work IS justified
